label: copy-phase input f (orig pos >= 2), boosted when next output is 0/f/y/1
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input token is f (100% of activations; never in the original or delimiter phase, never on any other input). It fires on only ~4% of copy-phase f inputs, though. Nearly all activations have recall_idx >= 3, meaning the f was original token 2 or later, with a peak at recall_idx 3-4. Activations are concentrated where the token being output right after the f is 0, f, y or 1 (85% of mass; out_tok 0 alone is 41%). prev_tok y gives a further boost. The strongest examples are "x y f 0" at original positions 2-3, e.g. 2 p y f 0 ... Activations are weak when f is at original position 1 or is followed by other tokens. Precision stays low: many copy-phase f inputs that meet these conditions are silent, especially late in long sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=f (+6.44), in_tok=f (+3.91), next_out=0 (+3.56), phase=2 & out_tok=0 (+3.28), out_tok=0 (+3.20), prev_tok=y (+2.94). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.53), recall_idx=1 (-2.78), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.78), out_tok=w (-2.22).
